# Access by role

Restricting documents and sections to the roles a signed identity carries, as the help article explains it to staff.

From the help article "Limit answers to some of your users" (`docs/help/knowledge/limit-answers-to-roles.md`, reviewed 2026-11-08). The same text answers in the Ask tab on opem.app.

## Can I give some documents only to some of my users?

Yes, on the Professional and Enterprise plans. Tag a document or a section with one or more roles, and the assistant answers from it only for people whose identity carries one of those roles. Every document is public until you tag it.

On Free and Basic the tags cannot be changed and the roles your app signs are not read, so anything tagged is hidden from everyone rather than shown to the wrong people. If you move to one of those plans with tags in place, the Knowledge page says how many documents and sections are hidden, with an Upgrade link; the tags stay, and answers from them come back when you upgrade.

The roles come from your own app: your server signs them into each person's identity, as it signs their id and email. Opem never decides who has a role; it only reads what your app sent.

## Do roles sent without a signature count?

Only when you switch on "Trust unsigned roles" on the Identity tab of the project's Configuration page. Then the roles your page passes to `Opem.identify()` without a signature open the documents tagged for them just as signed roles do, and the person's card in your inbox shows them marked "Unverified". With the switch off, the default, those roles are ignored and the person sees public documents only.

Think before switching it on: anyone who has your publishable key, which is in every page that loads the widget, can claim any role from their browser and read everything tagged for it. Keep it off, and sign identities, for material only some of your users may read.

## How do I tag a document?

Add `access` to its front matter with the roles that may read it, for example `access: [billing, admin]`. Anyone with either role gets answers from it; everyone else does not.

The front matter has to open the file: its first `---` goes at the top, with nothing but blank lines above it. If Opem finds an `access` line anywhere else above the first heading, it keeps the whole document out of answers and the Knowledge page names the line, so a misplaced tag never makes a document public.

You can also set the roles on the Knowledge page: open the document and use "+ role" under "Who can get answers from this document". For a document uploaded or written in Opem, this rewrites the `access` line in its front matter. For a document synced from your repository, the change lasts until the next sync, because the file in your repository always wins.

## How do I tag one section differently from the rest of its document?

Wrap the section, heading included, in an access tag: `{% access roles=["owner"] %}` on its own line before the heading and `{% /access %}` on its own line after the section. The sections inside take the tag's roles instead of the document's.

A tag can narrow a section (only owners may read it) or widen it: `{% access roles=[] %}` makes a section public inside a document tagged for a role.

Put the tag around whole sections. Text inside the tag before its first heading, or after the tag before the next heading, is kept out of answers, and the Knowledge page shows a warning naming the line.

## What happens if I make a mistake in a tag?

The tagged text is kept out of answers rather than shown to the wrong people. A role name that is not lower-case letters, digits, `-` or `_`, an access list that is not a list, a tag left unclosed or a tag inside a list or another tag all remove what they cover. The sync result, the editor and the notice at the top of the Knowledge page say which document and which line.

## What does the Roles tab do?

It lists the roles your app sends, with how many documents and sections each one is used in. Add a role there when your app starts sending it.

A role used in a tag but missing from the list is marked "Not on the list". That usually means a misspelt tag: if your app never sends that role, nobody can read what the tag covers. The list never changes a tag, and a tag naming an unlisted role still works.

Owners and admins can change the list and the tags. Agents can see them, and can edit a tagged document as long as they leave its tags as they are.

## What do people without the role see?

They get the answer they would get if the documentation did not cover their question: the assistant says it cannot help with that here and offers to send a request, with their question already filled in. The assistant never sees the hidden text, so it cannot quote it, hint at it or mention that it exists.

People who are not signed in, and people whose identity is not signed by your server, get public documents only, unless you trust unsigned roles (above).

## How do I check what a role can read?

Open a document and use "Try as a role" under its sections: choose a role, and the page says how many sections that role can read and which stay hidden.

To try the whole assistant, use the test console on the Assistant page and choose roles under "Try as a role" before you ask. The console asks exactly as someone your server signed with those roles, and its details show how many sections were kept back.
